Drivers must use due care to avoid hitting people, bicyclists, animals or other vehicles and slow or stop when circumstances require. People walking or bicycling near the road, animals, railroad crossings, intersections, bridges, curves and steep descents call for extra caution. Following distance must be reasonable and prudent for the speed, traffic and road conditions. On a two-lane road outside an urban area, safely pull over when at least five vehicles are immediately behind you. For the recommended four-second following gap, begin counting when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point and reach that point only after the count ends. Increase the recommended following gap to at least six seconds when towing a trailer or driving on a wet or slippery surface. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. The manual distinguishes its four-second recommendation from a stated legal minimum of two seconds. Watch brake lights and move a foot promptly toward the brake so you are ready to stop. A shrinking gap to the vehicle ahead warns of a possible rear-end collision. Compare distant vehicles with fixed surroundings to judge whether they are moving or stopped. Anticipating problems faced by the driver ahead gives more time to react. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Choose and manage speed for actual road, traffic and weather conditions. Unless another limit is posted or lawfully established, the favorable-condition maximum in an alley is fifteen miles per hour. narration.text: Unless another limit is posted or lawfully established, the favorable-condition maximum in a school zone is twenty miles per hour. Unless another limit is posted or lawfully established, the favorable-condition maximum in a residential district is twenty-five miles per hour. The favorable-condition maximum for another otherwise-unposted roadway is fifty-five miles per hour; selected highways may be posted at sixty-five miles per hour. Local authorities or the state transportation department may alter speed limits. A careful and prudent speed must account for traffic, traction, roadway width, weather and visibility when conditions are unfavorable. The manual requires moving over to give emergency vehicles on the shoulder additional protection. Traffic-offense fines are doubled in designated traffic safety corridors.
